verses.text: One day Peter and John were going up to the temple at three in the afternoon, the time for prayer.
A man who had been lame from birth was being carried there. Every day people put him by the temple gate called Beautiful, so he could beg from those going into the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to go in, he asked them for money.
Peter looked straight at him, and so did John. Then Peter said, "Look at us."
So the man looked at them, hoping to get something from them.
But Peter said, "I have no silver or gold, but I will give you what I do have. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!"
Peter took him by the right hand and helped him up. At once the man's feet and ankles became strong.
He jumped up, stood, and began to walk. Then he went into the temple with them, walking, jumping, and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God.
They knew he was the man who used to sit and beg at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. They were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
The man held on to Peter and John, and all the people ran to them in the place called Solomon's Porch. They were greatly amazed.
When Peter saw this, he said to them, "Men of Israel, why are you surprised at this? Why do you stare at us, as if we made this man walk by our own power or goodness?

The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our ancestors, has given glory to his servant Jesus. You handed him over and rejected him in front of Pilate, even when Pilate had decided to let him go.
You rejected the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a murderer to be set free instead.
You killed the one who gives life, but God raised him from the dead. We are witnesses of this.
It is by faith in the name of Jesus that this man you see and know has been made strong. Faith that comes through Jesus has made him completely well, as you can all see.
"Now, brothers, I know that you did this without understanding, and so did your leaders.
But this is how God made happen what he had told through all his prophets: that his Christ would suffer.
"So turn away from your sins and turn back to God, so that your sins may be wiped away. Then times of refreshing will come from the Lord,
and he will send Jesus, the Christ he chose for you.
Jesus must stay in heaven until the time comes for God to make all things new, as he promised long ago through his holy prophets.
Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people. You must listen to everything he tells you.
Anyone who does not listen to that prophet will be completely cut off from God's people.'
"Yes, all the prophets from Samuel on, all who have spoken, also told about these days.
You are the children of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your ancestors. He said to Abraham, 'Through your descendants all the families of the earth will be blessed.'
God raised up his servant and sent him first to you, to bless you by turning each of you away from your evil ways."
